title: Attend interaction UI: endpoint + HTMX button + HX-Trigger
description:
Design ref: docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.4-map-invite-design.md §Follow-and-attend-interactions Depends on: kb-2eu.3 (Attendance model must exist) **URL pattern** — add to /workspace/events/urls.py after existing entries: path('/attend/', views.event_attend, name='event-attend'), Note: existing entries are '', '/drawer/', and '//'. The new attend path uses an integer PK and does not conflict with any existing pattern. URL ordering: the int:event_id pattern is distinguishable from slug:org_slug by type, but Django matches in order — place the attend path after the drawer path and before the detail path to be safe. **View** — add to /workspace/events/views.py after event_detail view (currently ends at line 172). Add to the existing import lines at top of views.py: from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required View function to add: @require_POST @login_required def event_attend(request, event_id): event = get_object_or_404(Event, pk=event_id, status='published') status_val = request.POST.get('status', 'interested') if status_val not in ('interested', 'going', 'went'): status_val = 'interested' # Guard: 'went' only allowed after event.start has passed if status_val == 'went' and event.start > timezone.now(): status_val = 'going' attendance, created = Attendance.objects.update_or_create( user=request.user, event=event, defaults={'status': status_val}, ) event_past = event.start < timezone.now() response = render(request, 'events/_attend_button.html', { 'event': event, 'attendance': attendance, 'event_past': event_past, }) response['HX-Trigger'] = 'events:attendance-changed' return response Note: timezone is already imported at line 7 of events/views.py. Attendance is imported in kb-2eu.3 (added to 'from .models import Event, Tag, Attendance'). get_object_or_404 is already imported at line 5 of views.py. **Error paths:** - Non-existent event_id: get_object_or_404 raises 404. Returns HTTP 404. Correct. - Unpublished event (status != 'published'): get_object_or_404 raises 404 (status='published' filter). Returns HTTP 404. Correct. - Invalid status value (not in choices): clamped to 'interested'. No error response — silently corrects. This is intentional defensive behaviour. - 'went' on future event: clamped to 'going'. No error response — silently corrects. - Unauthenticated POST: @login_required redirects to /accounts/login/ (302). Correct. - CSRF missing: Django's CSRF middleware returns 403 before the view runs. Correct. **State transitions:** - No previous Attendance row → created with status_val. (Attendance.objects.update_or_create creates new row.) - Existing row, any status → updated to status_val. (update_or_create updates existing row.) - interested → going: valid, creates or updates row. - going → interested: valid, updates row. - going → went: only allowed when event_past=True (event.start < now). If event is future, clamped to 'going'. - Double-click same button: idempotent (update_or_create with same status_val updates updated_at but status unchanged). **HTMX partial template** — create /workspace/templates/events/_attend_button.html: {% load i18n %}
{% csrf_token %} {% if event_past %} {% endif %}
Note: event_past is a Python boolean passed from the view — do not use Django's {% now %} tag for time comparison. When attendance is None (first visit, no existing row), both Interested and Going buttons render without btn-active class. The {% if attendance and ... %} check handles None safely. **Include the partial in /workspace/templates/events/detail.html:** The tags block ends at line 58 ({% endif %} closing {% if event.tags.all %}). The description block begins at line 60. Insert between them (after line 58, before line 60): {% if user.is_authenticated and MAP_ENABLED %} {% include 'events/_attend_button.html' with event=event attendance=attendance event_past=event_past %} {% endif %} The MAP_ENABLED flag comes from the feature_flags context processor (added in kb-2eu.1). Per the design doc, attend/follow buttons are gated by MAP_ENABLED. The attendance and event_past variables come from the updated event_detail view (see below). **Update event_detail view** (/workspace/events/views.py lines 155-172) to compute attendance and event_past: if request.user.is_authenticated: try: attendance = Attendance.objects.get(user=request.user, event=event) except Attendance.DoesNotExist: attendance = None else: attendance = None event_past = event.start < timezone.now() Add attendance and event_past to context dict. **Map integration — bridge.js ADR-004 D3 compliance** (/workspace/static/js/events/bridge.js): When the server sends HX-Trigger: events:attendance-changed, HTMX automatically dispatches a DOM event named 'events:attendance-changed' on document.body. Listen for this event directly rather than manually reading response headers — this is the correct ADR-004 D3 event-bus pattern. Add after the existing htmx:afterSwap listener (after line 26): // When user marks attendance on a private-venue event, re-fetch markers // so exact coords are shown if user just marked 'going'. ADR-004 D3: event-bus. document.body.addEventListener('events:attendance-changed', function () { window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('events:filter-changed', {})) }) This re-uses the existing events:filter-changed machinery (bridge.js lines 22-25) to trigger a map marker refresh after an attendance change. **Done when:** 1. POST /events//attend/ with status=going updates or creates Attendance row and returns 200. 2. Response contains HX-Trigger: events:attendance-changed header. 3. 'Went' button does not appear in _attend_button.html when event_past=False. 4. Unauthenticated POST to /events//attend/ returns 302 to login page. 5. POST to non-existent event_id returns 404. 6. POST with status='went' on future event creates/updates row with status='going' (clamped). 7. _attend_button.html partial is included in detail.html only when user is authenticated and MAP_ENABLED=True. 8. bridge.js dispatches events:filter-changed when 'events:attendance-changed' event fires on document.body. 9. Repeat POST with same status is idempotent (200 response, single Attendance row, status unchanged). **Verification:** - pytest tests/ -k 'attend' — attend endpoint tests pass. - Manual: click Interested on a published event, verify Attendance row in Django admin, verify HX-Trigger header in browser devtools Network tab.

description:
Design ref: docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.4-map-invite-design.md §Invite-flow and §Data-model-deltas

Depends on: kb-2eu.1 (context processor must exist for INVITES_ENABLED; middleware relaxed for approved users)

**InviteCode model** — append after User class in /workspace/accounts/models.py:

  import secrets

  def generate_code():
      return secrets.token_urlsafe(24)  # ~32 chars, 192 bits entropy

  class InviteCode(models.Model):
      code = models.CharField(max_length=48, unique=True, default=generate_code)
      created_by = models.ForeignKey(
          settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.PROTECT,
          related_name='invites_created'
      )
      created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
      redeemed_by = models.ForeignKey(

          on_delete=models.SET_NULL, related_name='invite_redeemed'
      )
      redeemed_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
      expires_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
      notes = models.TextField(blank=True)

      def __str__(self):
          return self.code[:12]

Also add 'from django.conf import settings' import at top of /workspace/accounts/models.py (not currently imported).
Also add 'import secrets' at top of /workspace/accounts/models.py.

**Migration:** python manage.py makemigrations accounts
Produces: /workspace/accounts/migrations/0002_invitecode.py (next after existing 0001_initial.py)

**NoSignupAdapter override** (/workspace/accounts/adapter.py):
Allauth version in this project: check with 'pip show django-allauth | grep Version'. The override signatures below are compatible with allauth >=65.0.
The existing NoSignupAdapter has only is_open_for_signup. Add two overrides:

1. Replace is_open_for_signup(self, request) entirely:
  from django.conf import settings
  from django.utils import timezone

  def is_open_for_signup(self, request):
      if not getattr(settings, 'INVITES_ENABLED', True):
          return False
      code = request.GET.get('code') or request.session.get('invite_code')
      if not code:
          return False
      from accounts.models import InviteCode
      try:
          invite = InviteCode.objects.get(code=code, redeemed_by__isnull=True)
      except InviteCode.DoesNotExist:
          return False
      if invite.expires_at and invite.expires_at <= timezone.now():
          return False
      request.session['invite_code'] = code
      return True

2. Add save_user override. Signature: save_user(self, request, user, form, commit=True).
The code redemption must be atomic to handle a race where two requests redeem the same code simultaneously.
Strategy: call super() first (saves the user), then atomically mark the code redeemed via a filtered UPDATE.
If updated == 0, the code was already taken — delete the newly-created user and raise ValidationError.

Note on error path: allauth calls save_user inside its signup view's form.save() path. Raising django.forms.ValidationError from save_user is NOT caught by allauth's form validation layer — it will propagate as an unhandled 500 error unless the signup view has a try/except. To handle this gracefully, re-raise as a django.core.exceptions.ValidationError (not django.forms.ValidationError) so Django's middleware can convert it, OR add a top-level try/except in the view. The safe approach for 0.4 scale: log the race condition and return the user object without redemption (the invite code stays unredeemed but no 500 occurs). A staff member can manually clean up. If strict rejection is required, use django.forms.ValidationError and add a test for the 500-vs-400 behaviour. For now, use the lenient approach:

  from django.db import transaction
  import logging
  logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

  def save_user(self, request, user, form, commit=True):
      user = super().save_user(request, user, form, commit=commit)
      if commit:
          code = request.session.get('invite_code')
          if code:
              from django.utils import timezone as tz
              from accounts.models import InviteCode
              with transaction.atomic():
                  updated = InviteCode.objects.filter(
                      code=code, redeemed_by__isnull=True
                  ).update(redeemed_by=user, redeemed_at=tz.now())
                  if updated == 0:
                      # Race: code already redeemed. Log and continue (lenient).
                      # The new user account is created but invite code is not marked.
                      # Staff can reconcile. At 0.4 scale (5-15 users) this is acceptable.
                      logger.warning(
                          'Invite code %s already redeemed when saving user %s',
                          code, user.pk
                      )
              request.session.pop('invite_code', None)
      return user

Note: User.is_approved defaults to False (already set in accounts/models.py line 7). No action needed for that field.

**Management command** — create directory structure and files:
  /workspace/accounts/management/__init__.py  (empty file)
  /workspace/accounts/management/commands/__init__.py  (empty file)
  /workspace/accounts/management/commands/generate_invite_codes.py

Command content:
  from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
  from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
  from accounts.models import InviteCode

  class Command(BaseCommand):
      help = 'Generate InviteCode rows'

      def add_arguments(self, parser):
          parser.add_argument('--count', type=int, default=1)
          parser.add_argument('--notes', type=str, default='')
          parser.add_argument('--created-by-username', type=str, required=True)

      def handle(self, *args, **options):
          User = get_user_model()
          creator = User.objects.get(username=options['created_by_username'])
          for _ in range(options['count']):
              invite = InviteCode.objects.create(
                  created_by=creator,
                  notes=options['notes'],
              )
              self.stdout.write(invite.code)

Error path: if --created-by-username does not exist, User.objects.get raises User.DoesNotExist. This propagates as an unhandled CommandError-like traceback. This is acceptable for a staff-only management command — no additional handling needed.

**Admin** (/workspace/accounts/admin.py):
Current line 5: from .models import User
Change to: from .models import User, InviteCode

Add after existing CustomUserAdmin class (after line 14):

  @admin.register(InviteCode)
  class InviteCodeAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
      list_display = ['code', 'created_by', 'created_at', 'redeemed_by', 'redeemed_at', 'expires_at']
      list_filter = ['redeemed_by']
      readonly_fields = ['code', 'redeemed_by', 'redeemed_at', 'created_at']

**Done when:**
1. python manage.py generate_invite_codes --count 3 --notes test --created-by-username admin creates 3 InviteCode rows and prints each code.
2. GET /accounts/signup/?code=VALID_CODE renders the signup form (is_open_for_signup returns True).
3. Successful signup with valid code sets redeemed_by on InviteCode row; new user.is_approved=False.
4. GET /accounts/signup/ without code: is_open_for_signup returns False (allauth shows closed page).
5. Expired code (expires_at in the past) is rejected even if unredeemed.
6. Already-redeemed code (redeemed_by is set): GET /accounts/signup/?code=REDEEMED_CODE → is_open_for_signup returns False (allauth shows signup closed page, not a form).

**Error paths explicitly specified:**
- No code in URL or session → is_open_for_signup returns False (allauth shows closed page, not a crash).
- Invalid/unknown code → InviteCode.DoesNotExist → is_open_for_signup returns False.
- Already-redeemed code → redeemed_by__isnull=True filter fails → is_open_for_signup returns False.
- Expired code → expires_at check → is_open_for_signup returns False.
- Race condition (two requests with same code) → logged warning, both users created, invite code not double-marked (lenient; staff reconciles).

### 1. CREATE venues/tests/test_serializers.py

    from decimal import Decimal
    from django.test import TestCase
    from venues.models import Venue
    from venues.serializers import venue_to_geojson


    class VenueToGeoJSONPrivacyTest(TestCase):

        def test_public_venue_exact_coords(self):
            venue = Venue(slug='v1', latitude=Decimal('52.520000'), longitude=Decimal('13.400000'), privacy_mode='public')
            feature = venue_to_geojson(venue)
            self.assertEqual(feature['geometry']['type'], 'Point')
            self.assertEqual(feature['geometry']['coordinates'], [13.4, 52.52])
            self.assertEqual(feature['properties']['privacy'], 'public')

        def test_neighborhood_blur_rounds_to_3dp(self):
            venue = Venue(slug='v2', latitude=Decimal('52.520123'), longitude=Decimal('13.400456'), privacy_mode='neighborhood_blur', blur_radius_m=250)
            feature = venue_to_geojson(venue)
            self.assertEqual(feature['geometry']['coordinates'][1], round(52.520123, 3))
            self.assertEqual(feature['geometry']['coordinates'][0], round(13.400456, 3))
            self.assertEqual(feature['properties']['blur_radius_m'], 250)

        def test_private_venue_geometry_is_null(self):
            venue = Venue(slug='v3', latitude=Decimal('52.520000'), longitude=Decimal('13.400000'), privacy_mode='private')
            feature = venue_to_geojson(venue)
            self.assertIsNone(feature['geometry'], 'Exact coords must not be in GeoJSON for private venues')
            self.assertIn('fake_center', feature['properties'])
            self.assertEqual(feature['properties']['blur_radius_m'], 1000)

        def test_private_venue_fake_center_is_deterministic(self):
            venue = Venue(slug='v4', latitude=Decimal('52.520000'), longitude=Decimal('13.400000'), privacy_mode='private')
            f1 = venue_to_geojson(venue)
            f2 = venue_to_geojson(venue)
            self.assertEqual(f1['properties']['fake_center'], f2['properties']['fake_center'])

        def test_venue_with_null_coords_returns_none(self):
            venue = Venue(slug='v5', latitude=None, longitude=None, privacy_mode='public')
            self.assertIsNone(venue_to_geojson(venue))

Note: these tests do NOT save Venue to the database — Venue() without .save() is sufficient for the serializer since venue_to_geojson() only reads attributes, not the DB. This avoids needing the unique slug constraint.

### 2. CREATE events/tests/test_views_markers.py

    import json
    import re
    from decimal import Decimal
    from django.test import TestCase
    from django.utils import timezone
    from organizers.models import Organizer
    from venues.models import Venue
    from events.models import Event, Tag


    class EventListMarkersTest(TestCase):

        def setUp(self):
            self.organizer = Organizer.objects.create(
                name='Test Org',
                slug='test-org',
                status='approved',
            )
            self.venue_public = Venue.objects.create(
                name='Public Venue',
                slug='public-venue',
                latitude=Decimal('52.52'),
                longitude=Decimal('13.40'),
                privacy_mode='public',
            )
            self.venue_private = Venue.objects.create(
                name='Private Venue',
                slug='private-venue',
                latitude=Decimal('52.53'),
                longitude=Decimal('13.41'),
                privacy_mode='private',
            )
            self.tag_bdsm = Tag.objects.create(slug='bdsm', label='BDSM', kind='theme')
            now = timezone.now()

            self.events = []
            for i in range(2):
                event = Event.objects.create(
                    title=f'Public Event {i}',
                    slug=f'public-event-{i}',
                    organizer=self.organizer,
                    venue=self.venue_public,
                    start=now + timezone.timedelta(days=i + 1),
                    status='published',
                )
                event.tags.add(self.tag_bdsm)
                self.events.append(event)

            private_event = Event.objects.create(
                title='Private Event',
                slug='private-event',
                organizer=self.organizer,
                venue=self.venue_private,
                start=now + timezone.timedelta(days=3),
                status='published',
            )
            self.events.append(private_event)

        def test_markers_geojson_present_in_page_response(self):
            response = self.client.get('/events/')
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
            self.assertIn(b'markers-data', response.content)

        def test_tag_filter_returns_partial_with_server_timing(self):
            response = self.client.get('/events/', {'tags': 'bdsm'}, HTTP_HX_REQUEST='true')
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
            self.assertIn('Server-Timing', response)
            # Partial must not contain a full HTML document
            self.assertNotIn(b'<html', response.content.lower())

        def test_url_roundtrip_tags_param(self):
            response = self.client.get('/events/', {'tags': 'bdsm'})
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
            self.assertIn(b'bdsm', response.content)

        def test_private_venue_coords_absent_from_markers(self):
            response = self.client.get('/events/')
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
            content = response.content.decode()
            match = re.search(
                r'id="markers-data" type="application/json">(.*?)</script>',
                content,
                re.DOTALL,
            )
            self.assertIsNotNone(match, 'markers-data script tag not found in response')
            geojson = json.loads(match.group(1))
            private_features = [
                f for f in geojson['features']
                if f['properties'].get('privacy') == 'private'
            ]
            self.assertGreater(len(private_features), 0, 'Expected at least one private-venue feature')
            for f in private_features:
                self.assertIsNone(
                    f['geometry'],
                    f'Private venue geometry must be null, got {f["geometry"]}'
                )

        def test_drawer_returns_partial(self):
            event = self.events[0]
            response = self.client.get(f'/events/{event.pk}/drawer/')
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)
            self.assertNotIn(b'<html', response.content.lower())
            self.assertIn(event.title.encode(), response.content)

        def test_drawer_404_for_unknown_event(self):
            response = self.client.get('/events/999999/drawer/')
            self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 404)

## Run command

python manage.py test events.tests.test_views_markers venues.tests.test_serializers --verbosity=2

All tests must pass with no errors or failures.

- Private venue geometry is null in the markers payload (server privacy enforcement verified end-to-end)
- Drawer endpoint returns a fragment, not a full page
- HTMX partial response has Server-Timing header
- Null-coord venue returns None from serializer (does not crash the markers loop)
- Deterministic fake_center for private venues (same slug → same offset every time)

title: Seed data: extend with tags + pricing
description:
Extend events/management/commands/seed_spike_data.py to assign Tags to seeded events and set pricing fields. This unblocks tag-filter testing and price-filter testing during the spike.

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-20-phase-0.4-htmx-map-spike-design.md (section 'Out-of-spike prerequisites')

## What to change

File to modify: events/management/commands/seed_spike_data.py

### 1. Add tag fixture list at module level

After the existing constant blocks (before the Command class), add:

    _TAG_FIXTURES = [
        {'slug': 'bdsm',        'label': 'BDSM',         'kind': 'theme'},
        {'slug': 'rope',        'label': 'Rope',          'kind': 'theme'},
        {'slug': 'kink-social', 'label': 'Kink Social',   'kind': 'theme'},
        {'slug': 'sensation',   'label': 'Sensation',     'kind': 'theme'},
        {'slug': 'workshop',    'label': 'Workshop',      'kind': 'format'},
        {'slug': 'party',       'label': 'Party',         'kind': 'format'},
        {'slug': 'munch',       'label': 'Munch',         'kind': 'format'},
        {'slug': 'queer',       'label': 'Queer',         'kind': 'identity'},
        {'slug': 'femme',       'label': 'Femme',         'kind': 'identity'},
    ]

That is 9 tags across 3 kinds (theme, format, identity). The name _TAG_FIXTURES is referenced again in the wipe step — it must match exactly.

### 2. Update imports at the top of the file

Change:
    from events.models import Event
To:
    from events.models import Event, Tag

### 3. Create Tag rows in handle()

In handle(), after the guard/wipe block and before creating organizers, add:

    all_tags = []
    for t in _TAG_FIXTURES:
        tag, _ = Tag.objects.get_or_create(
            slug=t['slug'],
            defaults={'label': t['label'], 'kind': t['kind']},
        )
        all_tags.append(tag)

get_or_create is used (not create) so the command is idempotent if tags already exist in the DB from a previous run that didn't wipe them.

### 4. Assign tags to each event

In the inner event-creation loop, after the Event.objects.create(...) call, add:

    event.tags.set(rng.sample(all_tags, k=rng.randint(1, 3)))

The rng variable already exists in handle(). rng.sample draws without replacement; since all_tags has 9 items and k max is 3 this is safe.

### 5. Set pricing fields on each event

In the inner loop, before Event.objects.create(), determine pricing with the seeded RNG:

    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.40:
        is_free = True
        sliding_scale = False
        price_min = 0
        price_max = 0
    elif roll < 0.80:
        is_free = False
        sliding_scale = False
        price_min = rng.randint(500, 2000)
        price_max = price_min + rng.randint(0, 1000)
    else:
        is_free = False
        sliding_scale = True
        price_min = rng.randint(0, 500)
        price_max = rng.randint(1000, 3000)

Then pass these into Event.objects.create():
    Event.objects.create(
        title=title,
        slug=slug,
        organizer=org,
        venue=venue,
        start=start,
        status='published',
        is_free=is_free,
        sliding_scale=sliding_scale,
        price_min_cents=price_min,
        price_max_cents=price_max,
    )

### 6. Wipe: also delete seeded Tags

In the wipe branch (the 'if seed_data_exists and wipe:' block), before the existing Event.objects.filter(...).delete() line, add:

    Tag.objects.filter(slug__in=[t['slug'] for t in _TAG_FIXTURES]).delete()

Tag deletion does not cascade to events (M2M join rows are cleaned up automatically by Django when the Tag is deleted). Order: delete tags first, then events, then venues, then organizers.

## Verification

Run: python manage.py seed_spike_data --wipe
Expected stdout: 'Seeded 10 organizers, 60 venues, 540 events.'

Then in Django shell (python manage.py shell):
    from events.models import Event, Tag
    Tag.objects.count()  # should be 9
    Event.objects.filter(tags__isnull=False).distinct().count()  # should be 540 (all events get tags)
    Event.objects.filter(is_free=True).count()       # roughly 216 (40%)
    Event.objects.filter(sliding_scale=True).count() # roughly 108 (20%)

Run again with --wipe and confirm counts are the same (idempotency check).

title: Phase 0.3 integration test suite
description:

Design doc section: 'Test plan'

## Files to modify/create

- /workspace/tests/conftest.py (MODIFY — append new fixtures; existing fixtures must be preserved)
- /workspace/tests/integration/test_phase_0_3.py (NEW)

## tests/conftest.py — append fixtures

The current /workspace/tests/conftest.py has two fixtures: `superuser` and `isolate_logfire_token`.

## tests/integration/test_phase_0_3.py

Test style matches /workspace/tests/integration/test_phase_0_1.py:
- @pytest.mark.django_db decorator on each test
- `client` fixture from pytest-django (not Django's Client imported directly)
- `client.force_login(user)` for authentication
- Imports at module level where possible; model imports inside test bodies

```python
"""
Integration tests for Phase 0.3 — login-wall, views, filters, robots.txt.

Test plan items (from design doc):
- View smoke tests: /events, /events/<slug>, /o/<slug> return 200 for staff
- Login-wall: anon GET /events -> 302 to /accounts/login/
- Login-wall: non-staff authenticated user -> 403
- Signup closed: GET /accounts/signup/ -> not a working form (302 or 403)
- Filter correctness: ?tags=X filters queryset (OR semantics)
- Pagination + filter interaction: changing filter resets to page 1
- robots.txt: served disallow-all, no auth required
- X-Robots-Tag: present on all responses
- HTMX partial: HX-Request header returns partial not full HTML shell
"""

from datetime import timedelta

import django.utils.timezone as tz
import pytest


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Login-wall tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_loginwall_anon_redirects_to_login(client):
    """Anonymous GET /events/ -> 302 redirect to /accounts/login/."""
    response = client.get("/events/")
    assert response.status_code == 302
    assert "/accounts/login/" in response["Location"]


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_loginwall_anon_next_param(client):
    """Redirect includes ?next=/events/ so login returns user to intended page."""
    response = client.get("/events/")
    assert "next=" in response["Location"]


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_loginwall_nonstaff_gets_403(client, regular_user):
    """Authenticated non-staff user receives 403 from login-wall."""
    client.force_login(regular_user)
    response = client.get("/events/")
    assert response.status_code == 403


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_loginwall_staff_gets_through(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """Staff user can access /events/."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/")
    assert response.status_code == 200


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Signup closed
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_signup_closed(client):
    """GET /accounts/signup/ must not return a working form (302 or 403 expected)."""
    response = client.get("/accounts/signup/")
    assert response.status_code in (302, 403), (
        f"Expected 302 or 403 but got {response.status_code} — "
        "signup must be closed via NoSignupAdapter"
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# robots.txt
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_robots_txt_no_auth_required(client):
    """GET /robots.txt is in PUBLIC_PATHS — anon returns 200."""
    response = client.get("/robots.txt")
    assert response.status_code == 200


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_robots_txt_disallow_all(client):
    """robots.txt body disallows all crawlers."""
    response = client.get("/robots.txt")
    content = response.content.decode()
    assert "Disallow: /" in content


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# X-Robots-Tag header
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_x_robots_tag_on_login_page(client):
    """X-Robots-Tag header present on the login page itself."""
    response = client.get("/accounts/login/")
    assert "X-Robots-Tag" in response
    assert "noindex" in response["X-Robots-Tag"]


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_x_robots_tag_on_events_page(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """X-Robots-Tag header present on authenticated page responses."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/")
    assert "X-Robots-Tag" in response
    assert "noindex" in response["X-Robots-Tag"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# View smoke tests
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_event_list_smoke(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """GET /events/ returns 200 for staff user."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/")
    assert response.status_code == 200


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_event_detail_smoke(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """GET /events/<slug>/ returns 200 for staff user with published event."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get(f"/events/{published_event.slug}/")
    assert response.status_code == 200


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_event_detail_404_for_missing(client, staff_user):
    """GET /events/nonexistent/ returns 404."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/nonexistent-slug/")
    assert response.status_code == 404


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_organizer_profile_smoke(client, staff_user, approved_organizer, published_event):
    """GET /o/<slug>/ returns 200 for staff user with approved organizer."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get(f"/o/{approved_organizer.slug}/")
    assert response.status_code == 200


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_organizer_profile_404_for_missing(client, staff_user):
    """GET /o/nonexistent/ returns 404."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/o/nonexistent-organizer/")
    assert response.status_code == 404


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Filter correctness — OR semantics
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_filter_tags_or_semantics(client, staff_user, approved_organizer):
    """?tags=X,Y returns events tagged with X OR Y (union, not intersection)."""
    from events.models import Event, Tag

    tag_a = Tag.objects.create(slug="tag-a", label="Tag A", kind="theme")
    tag_b = Tag.objects.create(slug="tag-b", label="Tag B", kind="theme")

    future = tz.now() + timedelta(days=5)
    event_a = Event.objects.create(
        title="Event A",
        slug="event-a",
        organizer=approved_organizer,
        status="published",
        start=future,
    )
    event_a.tags.add(tag_a)

    event_b = Event.objects.create(
        title="Event B",
        slug="event-b",
        organizer=approved_organizer,
        status="published",
        start=future + timedelta(hours=1),
    )
    event_b.tags.add(tag_b)

    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/?tags=tag-a,tag-b")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    content = response.content.decode()
    assert "Event A" in content
    assert "Event B" in content


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_filter_unknown_tag_silently_ignored(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """?tags=nonexistent-tag returns 200 without crashing."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/?tags=this-tag-does-not-exist")
    assert response.status_code == 200


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_filter_price_free(client, staff_user, approved_organizer):
    """?price=free returns only free events, excludes paid events."""
    from events.models import Event

    future = tz.now() + timedelta(days=5)
    Event.objects.create(
        title="Free Event",
        slug="free-event",
        organizer=approved_organizer,
        status="published",
        start=future,
        is_free=True,
    )
    Event.objects.create(
        title="Paid Event",
        slug="paid-event",
        organizer=approved_organizer,
        status="published",
        start=future + timedelta(hours=1),
        is_free=False,
        price_min_cents=1500,
    )

    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/?price=free")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    content = response.content.decode()
    assert "Free Event" in content
    assert "Paid Event" not in content


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_filter_bad_date_falls_back_gracefully(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """?from=not-a-date returns 200 (invalid date silently ignored, no crash)."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/?from=not-a-date")
    assert response.status_code == 200


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_filter_bad_page_falls_back_to_1(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """?page=banana returns 200 (invalid page falls back to page 1)."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/?page=banana")
    assert response.status_code == 200


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pagination + filter interaction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_pagination_preserves_filter_params(client, staff_user, approved_organizer):
    """Pagination links include filter query params.

    Creates 25 published future events (> page size of 20) all tagged with tag-c,
    requests page 2 with ?tags=tag-c, and verifies 200 + the tag param is preserved
    in the rendered pagination HTML.
    """
    from events.models import Event, Tag

    tag = Tag.objects.create(slug="tag-c", label="Tag C", kind="theme")
    future = tz.now() + timedelta(days=1)
    events = []
    for i in range(25):
        e = Event.objects.create(
            title=f"Paginated Event {i}",
            slug=f"paginated-event-{i}",
            organizer=approved_organizer,
            status="published",
            start=future + timedelta(hours=i),
        )
        e.tags.add(tag)
        events.append(e)

    client.force_login(staff_user)
    # Page 2 with filter — should return 200 and contain pagination links preserving tags=tag-c
    response = client.get("/events/?tags=tag-c&page=2")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    content = response.content.decode()
    # Pagination links should reference tags=tag-c
    assert "tags=tag-c" in content


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HTMX partial rendering
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_htmx_partial_response(client, staff_user, published_event):
    """HTMX request (HX-Request header) returns partial, not full HTML shell."""
    client.force_login(staff_user)
    response = client.get("/events/", HTTP_HX_REQUEST="true")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    content = response.content.decode()
    assert "<!DOCTYPE html>" not in content
    assert "<html" not in content
```

## Known constraints

- `published_event` fixture creates Event with slug="test-event" under `approved_organizer`.
  Tests that create additional events in the same test must use different slug values
  (UniqueConstraint on organizer+slug) AND different (start, title) combinations
  (UniqueConstraint on organizer+start+title). The filter tests above satisfy both by using
  different slugs ("event-a", "event-b", etc.) and time offsets (timedelta(hours=1)).

- The `test_filter_tags_or_semantics`, `test_filter_price_free`, and
  `test_pagination_preserves_filter_params` tests do NOT use the `published_event` fixture
  (they create their own events) to avoid slug conflicts.

- Event page size is 20 (per views.py Paginator(qs, 20)). The pagination test creates 25 events
  to force a second page.

## Done-when

- All tests in test_phase_0_3.py pass with python -m pytest tests/integration/test_phase_0_3.py
- python -m pytest tests/ -x passes (existing phase 0.1 suite still green)

## Verification commands

```bash
cd /workspace
python -m pytest tests/integration/test_phase_0_3.py -v
python -m pytest tests/ -x -q
```

title: Event detail and organizer profile views
Event list view with HTMX filters
description:
Implement the /events list view with HTMX-driven filter chips, URL-synced query params, partial rendering, and pagination. Depends on bead 1 (kb-csd.1) for routing and login-wall infrastructure. Design doc section: '/events list view', 'Filter contract', 'Templates + Cotton components' ## Files to create/modify - /workspace/events/views.py (REPLACE — current file has only a comment; replace entire file) - /workspace/templates/events/list.html (NEW — create directory first: mkdir -p /workspace/templates/events) - /workspace/templates/cotton/event_card.html (NEW) - /workspace/templates/cotton/filter_chips.html (NEW) - /workspace/templates/cotton/pagination.html (NEW) - /workspace/templates/_base.html (MODIFY — add hx-headers CSRF attribute to body tag) ## _base.html change Current line 25 in /workspace/templates/_base.html: Change to: This establishes the CSRF pattern for 0.4 mutating HTMX interactions. ## events/views.py — replace entire file Current /workspace/events/views.py contains only `# Create your views here.` — replace the entire file. ```python import urllib.parse from django.core.paginator import Paginator from django.http import HttpResponse from django.shortcuts import get_object_or_404, render from django.utils import timezone from django.utils.dateparse import parse_date from .models import Event, Tag def event_list(request): now = timezone.now() qs = ( Event.objects.filter(status="published", start__gte=now) .select_related("organizer", "venue") .prefetch_related("tags") .order_by("start") ) # Filter: tags (OR semantics, comma-separated slugs) tags_param = request.GET.get("tags", "") tag_slugs = [s.strip() for s in tags_param.split(",") if s.strip()] if tag_slugs: valid_slugs = list( Tag.objects.filter(slug__in=tag_slugs).values_list("slug", flat=True) ) if valid_slugs: qs = qs.filter(tags__slug__in=valid_slugs).distinct() # Filter: from / to date from_param = request.GET.get("from", "") to_param = request.GET.get("to", "") if from_param: from_date = parse_date(from_param) if from_date: qs = qs.filter(start__date__gte=from_date) if to_param: to_date = parse_date(to_param) if to_date: qs = qs.filter(start__date__lte=to_date) # Filter: organizer slug organizer_param = request.GET.get("organizer", "") if organizer_param: qs = qs.filter(organizer__slug=organizer_param) # Filter: price price_param = request.GET.get("price", "") if price_param == "free": qs = qs.filter(is_free=True) elif price_param == "paid": qs = qs.filter(is_free=False) # Pagination — invalid page falls back to page 1 try: page_num = int(request.GET.get("page", 1)) except (ValueError, TypeError): page_num = 1 paginator = Paginator(qs, 20) page_obj = paginator.get_page(page_num) all_tags = Tag.objects.all().order_by("kind", "label") # Build filter query string for pagination links (excludes 'page' param) filter_params = {} if tag_slugs: filter_params["tags"] = ",".join(tag_slugs) if from_param: filter_params["from"] = from_param if to_param: filter_params["to"] = to_param if organizer_param: filter_params["organizer"] = organizer_param if price_param: filter_params["price"] = price_param filter_query_string = urllib.parse.urlencode(filter_params) context = { "page_obj": page_obj, "all_tags": all_tags, "active_tag_slugs": tag_slugs, "from_param": from_param, "to_param": to_param, "organizer_param": organizer_param, "price_param": price_param, "filter_query_string": filter_query_string, } if request.htmx: return render(request, "events/list.html#event_list", context) return render(request, "events/list.html", context) def event_detail(request, slug): # Stub — replaced in bead 3 (kb-csd.3) return HttpResponse("stub") ``` Notes: - `import urllib.parse` is at the top of the file — do not omit it. - `get_object_or_404` is imported here (used by bead 3's replacement of event_detail — importing it now avoids the bead 3 agent needing to add it mid-file). - `request.htmx` is provided by django-htmx middleware (confirmed in MIDDLEWARE at line 72). - `"events/list.html#event_list"` renders only the partialdef block named event_list. - `select_related` + `prefetch_related` is REQUIRED per design doc to avoid N+1 queries. - `parse_date` is imported at module level (not inside try blocks). - `filter_query_string` is built after all filter params are resolved and added to context. ## templates/events/list.html Create directory: mkdir -p /workspace/templates/events Uses template_partials (confirmed installed: template_partials.apps.SimpleAppConfig in INSTALLED_APPS, template_partials.loader.Loader in TEMPLATES loaders, template_partials.templatetags.partials in builtins). The partialdef block wraps the list and pagination. ```html {% extends "_base.html" %} {% load i18n %} {% block title %}{% trans "Events" %} — Kinky Bubbles{% endblock %} {% block layout %}

{% trans "Events" %}

{% partialdef event_list inline %}
{% for event in page_obj %} {% empty %}

{% trans "No events found." %}

{% endfor %}
{% endpartialdef %}
{% endblock %} ``` IMPORTANT Cotton prop syntax: use `:prop="variable"` (colon prefix) to pass Python objects (querysets, lists, model instances) into Cotton components. Without the colon prefix, Cotton renders the value as a template string. ## templates/cotton/event_card.html This component receives a single `event` model instance via `:event="event"`. ```html {% load i18n %}

{{ event.title }}

{% if event.organizer %}

{{ event.organizer.name }}

{% endif %}

{{ event.start|date:"D, d M Y, H:i" }}

{% if event.venue %}

{{ event.venue.name }}

{% endif %}
{% if event.is_free %} {% trans "Free" %} {% elif event.price_min_cents %} {{ event.currency }} {{ event.price_min_cents }}+ {% endif %}
``` ## templates/cotton/filter_chips.html Receives Python objects via colon-prefix props. RECOMMENDED implementation uses Alpine.js for correct tag toggle (add/remove) behavior. Django templates cannot do set subtraction inline cleanly — Alpine handles this correctly. Alpine.js is already loaded in _base.html line 21. ```html {% load i18n %}
{% for tag in all_tags %} {% endfor %} {# Hidden input carries final tag list to form submission #} {% if price_param == "free" %} {% else %} {% endif %}
``` Notes on filter_chips implementation: - `$el.closest('form')` — $el is Alpine's magic variable for the current element; `.closest('form')` traverses up the DOM to find the enclosing filter form; `.requestSubmit()` triggers the HTMX form submission (equivalent to clicking submit, fires the hx-trigger="change" handler). - `active_tag_slugs` is a Python list (e.g. `['tag-a', 'tag-b']`). The `|safe` filter renders it as a JS array literal in the x-data attribute. Verify in dev tools it renders as: `x-data="{ activeTags: ['tag-a'] }"` (with quotes around each slug). - The hidden `` is the single source of truth for the tags param submitted with the form. The tag buttons do NOT have name="tags" — only the hidden input does. - Page param is intentionally absent from all chip interactions — filter changes reset to page 1. - Alpine defers rendering until the DOM is ready. The x-data expression evaluates once; subsequent calls to toggle() update the reactive state and $el.closest('form').requestSubmit() fires the form. ## templates/cotton/pagination.html Receives page_obj via `:page_obj="page_obj"`. The `filter_query_string` value comes from the parent template context (Cotton components inherit the parent template context automatically — no need to pass it as a Cotton prop). ```html {% load i18n %} {% if page_obj.has_other_pages %}

{% endif %} ``` Note: `filter_query_string` is in the parent template context (passed from the view). ## accounts/middleware.py (replace entire file)

The existing file at /workspace/accounts/middleware.py contains only the ApprovalGateMiddleware
placeholder. Replace the entire file with LoginWallMiddleware.

```python
"""Accounts middleware for kinky-bubbles."""
from django.conf import settings
from django.http import HttpResponseForbidden
from django.shortcuts import redirect


class LoginWallMiddleware:
    """Hard login-wall for Phase 0.3 (staff-only).

    Anonymous users: redirect to /accounts/login/?next=<path>.
    Authenticated non-staff: 403 (will relax to is_approved at 0.4).
    Adds X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow, noarchive to every response.
    Kill-switch: LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED=False in settings bypasses the wall.
    """

    PUBLIC_PATHS = {"/accounts/login/", "/accounts/logout/", "/healthz", "/robots.txt"}

    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        if not getattr(settings, "LOGIN_WALL_ENABLED", True):
            response = self.get_response(request)
            response["X-Robots-Tag"] = "noindex, nofollow, noarchive"
            return response
        if request.path not in self.PUBLIC_PATHS and not request.user.is_authenticated:
            return redirect(f"/accounts/login/?next={request.path}")
        if request.user.is_authenticated and not request.user.is_staff:
            return HttpResponseForbidden("Not available yet.")
        response = self.get_response(request)
        response["X-Robots-Tag"] = "noindex, nofollow, noarchive"
        return response
```

### Change 3: Replace the Docker Compose-based steps with direct uv steps
Remove: 'Set up Docker Compose', 'Build and start containers', 'Run tests', 'Run Ruff'
Replace with:

```yaml
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Install uv
      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: uv sync --frozen

    - name: Ruff lint
      run: uv run ruff check .

    - name: Ruff format check
      run: uv run ruff format --check .

    - name: djlint template check
      run: uv run djlint --check . --extension=html

    - name: Run migrations
      run: uv run python manage.py migrate

    - name: pytest
      run: uv run pytest

    - name: makemigrations check (no unapplied migrations)
      run: uv run python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run

    - name: makemessages check (i18n catalog not empty)
      run: |
        uv run python manage.py makemessages -l de
        if ! grep -q '^msgid ' locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.po; then
          echo 'ERROR: locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/django.po is empty — add {% trans %} tags to templates'
          exit 1
        fi
```

### Change 4: Set environment variables at job level (not per-step)
```yaml
    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres
      SECRET_KEY: ci-insecure-key-for-testing-only
      DEBUG: 'True'
      ALLOWED_HOSTS: 'localhost,127.0.0.1,testserver'
      LOGFIRE_TOKEN: ''
```

## MAKEMESSAGES EMPTY CATALOG TRAP
django-admin makemessages -l de only produces non-empty output if at least one {% trans %} or _() call exists in the codebase. If no trans tags exist when this step runs, the .po file header exists but has no msgid lines, and the CI check above fails. Ensure at least one {% trans %} tag exists in a template before this CI step can go green. The admin customizations in bead B may produce some strings via verbose_name or short_description, but template tags are needed for the grep check. title: C. django-q2 heartbeat task + 5-minute schedule
description:
Wire a real heartbeat task into django-q2 that proves the worker loop is alive. This is the go/no-go gate for phase 0.2.

Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.1-schema-admin-design.md, section: django-q2 heartbeat, Test plan.

## Context
settings.py already has Q_CLUSTER configured with orm='default'. ingestion/models.py (from bead B) has HeartbeatLog(ran_at, note). This bead adds the task function and the Schedule entry.

## What to do

### 1. ingestion/tasks.py
Create this file:

import logfire
from django.utils import timezone
from .models import HeartbeatLog

def heartbeat():
    """Inserted every 5 minutes by django-q2 scheduler. Proves worker loop is alive."""
    log = HeartbeatLog.objects.create(note='scheduled heartbeat')
    logfire.info('heartbeat ok', heartbeat_log_id=log.pk, ran_at=log.ran_at.isoformat())

### 2. Schedule via django-q2 Schedule model
In a data migration or a management command — the cleanest approach for 0.1 is a management command that seeds the schedule (idempotent, safe to re-run):

Create ingestion/management/__init__.py, ingestion/management/commands/__init__.py, ingestion/management/commands/seed_q_schedule.py:

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django_q.models import Schedule

class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = 'Seed django-q2 schedule entries (idempotent)'

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        Schedule.objects.update_or_create(
            name='heartbeat',
            defaults=dict(
                func='ingestion.tasks.heartbeat',
                schedule_type=Schedule.MINUTES,
                minutes=5,
                repeats=-1,  # repeat forever
            ),
        )
        self.stdout.write(self.style.SUCCESS('Schedule seeded: heartbeat every 5 minutes'))

### 3. Logfire dependency
logfire>=3.0 is already in pyproject.toml dependencies — no uv add needed. Import pattern in tasks.py is: import logfire (no config needed here; Logfire reads LOGFIRE_TOKEN env var at startup).

### 4. Verify locally (manual smoke test)
- Run: python manage.py seed_q_schedule
- Run qcluster in background: python manage.py qcluster &
- IMPORTANT: Wait at least 5 minutes (the schedule interval) before checking — HeartbeatLog rows do NOT appear immediately on qcluster startup, only after the first schedule interval fires.
- After 5+ minutes: python manage.py shell -c 'from ingestion.models import HeartbeatLog; print(HeartbeatLog.objects.count())'
- Should show >= 1

- Shortcut (no wait needed): call heartbeat() directly:
  python manage.py shell -c 'from ingestion.tasks import heartbeat; heartbeat(); from ingestion.models import HeartbeatLog; print(HeartbeatLog.objects.count())'
  Expected: 1

## Done when
- [ ] ingestion/tasks.py exists with heartbeat() function
- [ ] ingestion/management/commands/seed_q_schedule.py exists and is idempotent
- [ ] python manage.py seed_q_schedule runs without error
- [ ] HeartbeatLog row appears after direct call to ingestion.tasks.heartbeat() (fast path)
- [ ] HeartbeatLog row appears in DB after 5+ minutes of qcluster running (slow path / go-no-go gate)
- [ ] logfire import does not crash (package present in pyproject.toml)
notes:
VERIFICATION COMMANDS:

1. Management command runs idempotently:
   python manage.py seed_q_schedule
   Expected: 'Schedule seeded: heartbeat every 5 minutes'
   Run again: same output, no error, no duplicate rows.

2. Verify Schedule row exists:
   python manage.py shell -c "from django_q.models import Schedule; s = Schedule.objects.get(name='heartbeat'); print(s.func, s.minutes, s.repeats)"
   Expected: 'ingestion.tasks.heartbeat 5 -1'

3. Manual smoke test (requires running DB and qcluster):
   python manage.py qcluster &
   (Wait at least 5 minutes — the schedule is every 5 minutes, not every 10 seconds)
   python manage.py shell -c "from ingestion.models import HeartbeatLog; print(HeartbeatLog.objects.count())"
   Expected: >= 1

4. Shortcut smoke — call task directly without qcluster:
   python manage.py shell -c "from ingestion.tasks import heartbeat; heartbeat(); from ingestion.models import HeartbeatLog; print(HeartbeatLog.objects.count())"
   Expected: 1

TIMING NOTE: Step 3 requires waiting the full 5-minute schedule interval before HeartbeatLog rows appear. Do NOT check after 10 seconds — the first run fires after the first interval, not immediately on qcluster startup. Use step 4 (direct call) for a fast smoke test.

title: B. Domain schemas + admin: organizers, venues, events, ingestion, reviews
description:
Create all six domain apps with their models, migrations, and admin customizations. All model definitions are verbatim from the design doc. Design doc: docs/plans/2026-04-17-phase-0.1-schema-admin-design.md, sections: Data model, Admin customizations. ## Apps to create (all via python manage.py startapp ) - organizers/ - venues/ - events/ - ingestion/ - reviews/ Add all five to INSTALLED_APPS in a_core/settings.py (after 'accounts'). ## FK convention (critical) All FKs to the user model use the STRING 'settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL' resolved at runtime — never import the User class directly in models.py. Pattern: from django.conf import settings author = models.ForeignKey(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL, on_delete=models.CASCADE, ...) Cross-app FKs use string app_label.ModelName notation: raw_message = models.ForeignKey('ingestion.RawMessage', null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.SET_NULL) ## Models (exact field definitions in design doc — reproduce exactly) ### organizers/models.py — Organizer Fields: name, slug (unique), description, avatar (ImageField upload_to='organizers/'), website (URLField), telegram_channel. Trust tier: status (choices: candidate/approved/suspended, default=candidate), verified_badge (BooleanField default=False), approved_at (DateTimeField null/blank), approved_by (FK to settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL null/blank SET_NULL). GDPR consent (F5): consent_recorded_at (DateTimeField null/blank), consent_method (CharField choices: telegram_forward_implied / explicit_opt_in / verified_public_source, blank=True), consent_notes (TextField blank=True). Timestamps: created_at (auto_now_add), updated_at (auto_now). ### venues/models.py — Venue Fields: name, slug (unique), address (max_length=300 blank), neighborhood (max_length=100 blank). Geo (F4): latitude, longitude as DecimalField(max_digits=9, decimal_places=6, null=True, blank=True). Privacy: privacy_mode (choices: public / neighborhood_blur / private address on request, default=public), blur_radius_m (IntegerField default=250). Other: url (URLField blank), notes (TextField blank), created_at (auto_now_add). ### events/models.py — Tag Fields: slug (SlugField unique), label (max_length=100), kind (CharField choices: theme/format/identity/bubble), description (TextField blank). ### events/models.py — Event Fields: title (max_length=300), slug (SlugField max_length=200 — NOT globally unique, unique per organizer via constraint), description (TextField blank), organizer (FK Organizer PROTECT related_name=events), venue (FK Venue PROTECT null/blank related_name=events), tags (M2M Tag blank related_name=events). Time: start (DateTimeField), end (DateTimeField null/blank). Price: price_min_cents (IntegerField null/blank), price_max_cents (IntegerField null/blank), currency (max_length=3 default=EUR), is_free (BooleanField default=False), sliding_scale (BooleanField default=False). External: external_url (URLField blank), tickets_url (URLField blank). Lifecycle status (choices: draft/review/published/cancelled/rejected/archived, default=draft), published_at (DateTimeField null/blank). Provenance (F7): raw_message = FK('ingestion.RawMessage', null=True, blank=True, on_delete=SET_NULL). Timestamps: created_at (auto_now_add), updated_at (auto_now). class Meta: indexes = [Index(fields=['status','start']), Index(fields=['organizer','start'])] constraints = [ UniqueConstraint(fields=['organizer','slug'], name='event_slug_unique_per_organizer'), UniqueConstraint(fields=['organizer','start','title'], name='event_dup_guard_org_start_title'), ] ### events/models.py — EventImage Fields: event (FK Event CASCADE related_name=images), image (ImageField upload_to=events/), alt (max_length=300 blank), is_cover (BooleanField default=False), order (IntegerField default=0). ### ingestion/models.py — RawMessage Fields: source_type (CharField choices: telegram_bot_forward / telegram_telethon / email_submission / web_form), sender_id (max_length=100 blank), channel_id (max_length=100 blank), message_id (max_length=100 blank), received_at (auto_now_add), raw_payload (JSONField), text (TextField blank), enriched_payload (JSONField default=dict blank), extraction_status (CharField choices: pending/extracted/failed/skipped, default=pending), extraction_error (TextField blank). ### ingestion/models.py — SourceFailure Fields: source_type (max_length=50), raw_message (FK RawMessage null/blank SET_NULL), stage (max_length=50), error_class (max_length=200), error_message (TextField), occurred_at (auto_now_add), resolved (BooleanField default=False). ### ingestion/models.py — HeartbeatLog Fields: ran_at (auto_now_add), note (max_length=200 blank). ### reviews/models.py — Review Fields: author (FK settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL CASCADE related_name=reviews), organizer (FK Organizer null/blank CASCADE related_name=reviews), event (FK Event null/blank CASCADE related_name=reviews), rating (IntegerField validators=[MinValueValidator(1), MaxValueValidator(5)]), body (TextField blank), created_at (auto_now_add). class Meta: constraints = [ CheckConstraint( check=Q(organizer__isnull=False) ^ Q(event__isnull=False), name='review_targets_exactly_one', ), ] ## Migrations Run: python manage.py makemigrations organizers venues events ingestion reviews Run: python manage.py migrate All must succeed clean. ## Admin customizations (admin.py in each app) ### organizers/admin.py — OrganizerAdmin @admin.register(Organizer) class OrganizerAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['name', 'status', 'verified_badge', 'event_count'] list_filter = ['status', 'verified_badge'] search_fields = ['name', 'slug', 'telegram_channel'] readonly_fields = ['created_at', 'updated_at', 'approved_at'] actions = ['mark_approved_record_consent'] def event_count(self, obj): return obj.events.count() event_count.short_description = 'Events' @admin.action(description='Mark approved + record consent') def mark_approved_record_consent(self, request, queryset): from django.utils import timezone queryset.update( status='approved', approved_at=timezone.now(), approved_by=request.user, consent_recorded_at=timezone.now(), consent_method='explicit_opt_in', ) ### events/admin.py — EventAdmin + EventImageInline class EventImageInline(admin.TabularInline): model = EventImage extra = 0 @admin.register(Event) class EventAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['title', 'organizer', 'start', 'status'] list_filter = ['status', 'start', 'tags', 'organizer'] search_fields = ['title', 'description'] inlines = [EventImageInline] readonly_fields = ['created_at', 'updated_at', 'published_at', 'raw_message_preview'] actions = ['publish_events', 'reject_events', 'archive_events'] def raw_message_preview(self, obj): if not obj.raw_message: return '—' from django.utils.html import format_html return format_html('
{}
', obj.raw_message.text or str(obj.raw_message.raw_payload)) raw_message_preview.short_description = 'Raw message' @admin.action(description='Publish selected events') def publish_events(self, request, queryset): from django.utils import timezone queryset.update(status='published', published_at=timezone.now()) @admin.action(description='Reject selected events') def reject_events(self, request, queryset): queryset.update(status='rejected') @admin.action(description='Archive selected events') def archive_events(self, request, queryset): queryset.update(status='archived') ### ingestion/admin.py — RawMessageAdmin @admin.register(RawMessage) class RawMessageAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['source_type', 'received_at', 'extraction_status', 'text_preview'] list_filter = ['extraction_status'] readonly_fields = [f.name for f in RawMessage._meta.get_fields() if hasattr(f, 'name')] # all read-only in 0.1 def text_preview(self, obj): return obj.text[:80] if obj.text else '(no text)' text_preview.short_description = 'Text preview' ### reviews/admin.py — ReviewAdmin @admin.register(Review) class ReviewAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['author', 'target_display', 'rating', 'created_at'] def target_display(self, obj): if obj.organizer: return f'Organizer: {obj.organizer}' if obj.event: return f'Event: {obj.event}' return '(none)' target_display.short_description = 'Target' Also register Venue, Tag, EventImage with basic admin.register decorators. ## Done when - [ ] All 5 apps exist with models.py and admin.py - [ ] python manage.py makemigrations --check exits 0 (nothing unmigrated) - [ ] python manage.py migrate runs clean - [ ] All UniqueConstraints and CheckConstraint exist in migrations - [ ] python manage.py createsuperuser works and /admin/ loads all registered models - [ ] Organizer bulk action 'Mark approved + record consent' appears in admin - [ ] Event bulk actions publish/reject/archive appear in admin - [ ] RawMessageAdmin fields are all read-only in 0.1

VERIFICATION COMMANDS (run after all steps complete):

1. No unmigrated models:
   python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
   Expected: 'No changes detected' and exit 0.

2. Migrations apply cleanly:

3. Admin loads all registered models (requires superuser):

   Then run: python manage.py runserver and visit http://localhost:8000/admin/ — confirm organizer, venue, event, tag, eventimage, rawmessage, sourcefailure, review, heartbeatlog all appear.

4. Smoke-test each app's models import cleanly:
   python -c "from organizers.models import Organizer; from venues.models import Venue; from events.models import Event, Tag, EventImage; from ingestion.models import RawMessage, SourceFailure, HeartbeatLog; from reviews.models import Review; print('all imports ok')"
   Expected: 'all imports ok'

5. UniqueConstraints in migrations:
   python -c "from django.db import connection; cursor = connection.cursor(); cursor.execute(\"SELECT conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname IN ('event_slug_unique_per_organizer','event_dup_guard_org_start_title','review_targets_exactly_one');\"); print([r[0] for r in cursor.fetchall()])"
   Expected: list of 3 constraint names.

NOTE ON PER-APP TESTS: There are no per-app test directories in this project. All integration tests are in tests/test_phase_0_1.py (bead F). The done-when criterion 'pytest per-app smoke green' refers to the tests in bead F passing — run 'pytest tests/test_phase_0_1.py' after bead F is complete.

RAWMESSAGEADMIN READONLY FIX: Do NOT use the description's pattern (hasattr(f, 'name')). Use the NOTES-corrected pattern: readonly_fields = [f.name for f in RawMessage._meta.get_fields() if hasattr(f, 'column')] — this excludes reverse relations that have no column attribute and avoids AttributeError.

title: A. Foundation: custom User + AUTH_USER_MODEL + i18n wiring + vector extension
description:
Set up the foundational pieces that all other phase 0.1 beads depend on. Must be completed and migrated BEFORE any other app migration runs.

CRITICAL ORDER TRAP: AUTH_USER_MODEL must be set in settings.py before ANY migration runs. If migrations have already run with the default auth.User, switching is painful (Django trap). On a fresh repo/DB this is safe; verify no existing migrations in other apps before starting.

## Files to touch
- a_core/settings.py (AUTH_USER_MODEL, INSTALLED_APPS, MIDDLEWARE, i18n block)
- accounts/models.py (create)
- accounts/admin.py (create)
- accounts/migrations/0001_vector_extension.py (create by hand)
- accounts/migrations/0002_user.py (auto-generated, must depend on 0001)
- locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/ (create directory)

## Step 1: Create accounts app
Run from repo root (/Users/jonat/code/personal/kinky-bubbles):
  python manage.py startapp accounts

## Step 2: accounts/models.py
```python
from django.contrib.auth.models import AbstractUser
from django.db import models


class User(AbstractUser):
    is_approved = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    approved_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    approved_by = models.ForeignKey(
        'self',
        null=True,
        blank=True,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        related_name='approved_users',
    )
```

## Step 3: a_core/settings.py changes

### 3a. AUTH_USER_MODEL (add near top of file, before INSTALLED_APPS)
```python
AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'accounts.User'
```

### 3b. INSTALLED_APPS: add 'accounts' before 'pages'
```python
    # local
    'a_core',
    'accounts',
    'pages',
```

### 3c. MIDDLEWARE: add LocaleMiddleware immediately after SessionMiddleware (before CommonMiddleware)
Current order: SecurityMiddleware → WhiteNoise → SessionMiddleware → CommonMiddleware
Add: 'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware' between SessionMiddleware and CommonMiddleware.
Result:
```python
    'django.contrib.sessions.middleware.SessionMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware',
    'django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware',
```

### 3d. i18n settings block (add after USE_I18N = True line)
```python
LANGUAGES = [('en', 'English'), ('de', 'Deutsch')]
LOCALE_PATHS = [BASE_DIR / 'locale']
```
Note: USE_I18N, LANGUAGE_CODE, TIME_ZONE already set — do NOT duplicate them.

## Step 4: accounts/admin.py
```python
from django.contrib import admin
from django.contrib.auth.admin import UserAdmin

from .models import User


@admin.register(User)
class CustomUserAdmin(UserAdmin):
    fieldsets = UserAdmin.fieldsets + (
        ('Approval', {'fields': ('is_approved', 'approved_at', 'approved_by')}),
    )
    list_display = ['username', 'email', 'is_approved', 'is_staff']
```

## Step 5: Create locale directory
  mkdir -p locale/de/LC_MESSAGES

## Step 6: pgvector migration (HAND-WRITTEN — create before running makemigrations)
Create accounts/migrations/0001_vector_extension.py:
```python
from django.db import migrations


class Migration(migrations.Migration):
    dependencies = []

    operations = [
        migrations.RunSQL(
            sql='CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;',
            reverse_sql=migrations.RunSQL.noop,  # do NOT drop on reverse — data-loss risk on shared DB
        ),
    ]
```

## Step 7: Generate the User model migration
Run: python manage.py makemigrations accounts
This produces accounts/migrations/0002_user.py (or similar). Open that file and verify its dependencies list includes ('accounts', '0001_vector_extension'). If it was auto-numbered as 0001, rename 0001_vector_extension.py to be explicit and edit the auto-generated file's dependencies accordingly. The vector migration MUST come first.

## Step 8: Run migrations
Compose image must be pgvector/pgvector:pg17 (check docker-compose.yml before running).
Run: python manage.py migrate
Expected: all migrations apply cleanly, including CREATE EXTENSION.

## Done when
- [ ] AUTH_USER_MODEL = 'accounts.User' in a_core/settings.py
- [ ] python manage.py migrate runs clean on a fresh DB (pgvector/pgvector:pg17 image)
- [ ] CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector migration is the FIRST accounts migration (0001_*)
- [ ] Auto-generated User migration lists 0001_vector_extension as a dependency
- [ ] LocaleMiddleware in MIDDLEWARE between SessionMiddleware and CommonMiddleware
- [ ] LANGUAGES includes 'en' and 'de'; LOCALE_PATHS = [BASE_DIR / 'locale']
- [ ] locale/de/LC_MESSAGES/ directory exists
- [ ] python manage.py makemessages -l de runs without error (empty catalog is acceptable at this stage; a non-empty catalog is required after bead F ships)
notes:
VERIFICATION COMMANDS (run after all steps complete):

1. Fresh DB migration check:
   python manage.py migrate
   Expected: all migrations apply cleanly, no errors.

2. pgvector extension installed:
   psql $DATABASE_URL -c "SELECT * FROM pg_extension WHERE extname='vector';"
   Expected: one row returned.

3. AUTH_USER_MODEL correct:
   python -c "from django.conf import settings; assert settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL == 'accounts.User', settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL"
   Expected: no output (assertion passes).

4. LocaleMiddleware present:
   python -c "from django.conf import settings; assert 'django.middleware.locale.LocaleMiddleware' in settings.MIDDLEWARE, settings.MIDDLEWARE"
   Expected: no output (assertion passes).

5. i18n settings correct:
   python -c "from django.conf import settings; codes = [c for c,_ in settings.LANGUAGES]; assert 'en' in codes and 'de' in codes, codes"
   Expected: no output (assertion passes).

6. makemessages runs without error (non-empty catalog not required until bead D CI step goes green, but the command must exit 0):
   python manage.py makemessages -l de
   Expected: exit 0. An empty catalog is acceptable here — the CI enforcement of non-empty content is added in bead D and requires at least one {% trans %} tag in templates.

MIGRATION ORDER INVARIANT: Run 'python manage.py showmigrations accounts' and confirm 0001_vector_extension appears before 0002_user (or whatever Django auto-numbers the User migration). If they came out in wrong order, rename files and fix the dependencies list in the auto-generated file.

title: step-9b: week-off.md runbook
description:
Design: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-21-bundle-a-post-0.5-code-sprint-design.md#in-10-infra

Depends on: step-3 (finalize_attendance task ships and emits logfire metrics; week-off runbook references its health-check query).

Create /workspace/docs/runbooks/week-off.md. Pure documentation task — no code changes.

## Document to create

Create /workspace/docs/runbooks/week-off.md with these sections:

### Section 1: Pre-departure checklist
Before leaving for >= 5 days, verify:
- [ ] Last nightly run succeeded: check logfire for finalize_attendance.done and recompute_aggregates.done events from last 24h
- [ ] django-q2 cluster is running: docker ps or process check shows q-cluster active
- [ ] No unresolved flags with high severity in admin: /admin/reviews/flag/?resolved=False
- [ ] No EmailFailure rows from last 7 days: /admin/a_core/emailfailure/
- [ ] INGESTION_PAUSED=False (unless intentionally paused): /admin/a_core/featureflag/
- [ ] All feature flags are in intended state (review flag table in panic-mode.md)
- [ ] Django-q2 Schedule entries exist for both nightly tasks: python manage.py shell -c 'from django_q.models import Schedule; print(list(Schedule.objects.values("name","next_run")))'

### Section 2: What auto-heals while you're away
These are safe to leave running unattended:
- finalize_attendance (nightly 03:00 Europe/Berlin): flips going->went automatically. If it fails one night, it catches up on next run (idempotent).
- recompute_aggregates (nightly): recomputes all aggregate counts. If it fails one night, next run corrects it. Short-term display counts may be stale but no data loss.
- daily_flag_digest (daily): sends email digest. If SMTP fails, creates EmailFailure row. Non-critical; check on return.
- Telegram bot: continues ingesting if INGESTION_PAUSED=False. New events land as drafts and queue for admin review (no auto-publish). Safe to accumulate.

These require manual intervention if they fail:
- Admin event review queue (drafts do NOT auto-publish — maintainer must approve)
- FeatureFlag changes (must be manual)
- Any DSA takedown received via email (manual response required within 72h per DSA Art. 16)

### Section 3: On-return health check (logfire query)
Run these checks when returning from week off:

1. Did nightly tasks run every day?
   Logfire query to verify task history (adapt to logfire UI):

     SELECT DATE(timestamp), name, updated_count
     FROM logs
     WHERE name IN ('finalize_attendance.done', 'recompute_aggregates.done')
       AND timestamp > NOW() - INTERVAL '8 days'
     ORDER BY timestamp DESC

   Expected: at least one row per task per day. Zero rows for a day = task did not run (check q-cluster was alive).
   Note: both finalize_attendance and recompute_aggregates emit duration_ms alongside the count field — a healthy run shows non-null duration_ms.

2. Any email failures?
   Django shell: from a_core.models import EmailFailure; print(EmailFailure.objects.filter(resolved=False).count())
   Action: review and resolve if > 0.

3. Flag backlog?
   Django shell: from reviews.models import Flag; print(Flag.objects.filter(resolved=False).count())
   Action: triage via FlagAdmin moderation actions (step-6a).

4. Draft event backlog?
   Django shell: from events.models import Event; print(Event.objects.filter(status='draft').count())
   Action: review and approve/reject in admin.

### Section 4: Flags to flip before leaving (if going fully offline)
Optional hardening before a week off:
- INGESTION_PAUSED=True if you don't want new drafts accumulating
- FLAGS_ENABLED=False if you can't respond to flag volume
Restore on return: flip back, wait 60s cache TTL.

## Key files
- /workspace/docs/runbooks/week-off.md (new file)
- /workspace/docs/runbooks/ (shared directory with panic-mode.md from step-9a)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Contains pre-departure checklist with finalize_attendance health check
- Contains auto-heal inventory distinguishing tasks that self-recover vs require manual action
- Contains on-return logfire query for checking nightly task history — query selects both finalize_attendance.done and recompute_aggregates.done, filters last 8 days
- Both tasks' duration_ms field mentioned in the health-check section
- Contains flag recommendations for fully-offline period

## Verification

title: step-6b: Email digest enhancements
description:
Design: /workspace/docs/plans/2026-04-21-bundle-a-post-0.5-code-sprint-design.md#in-06a-machinery

Depends on: step-6a (FlagAdmin change_view must exist and consume ?action= param before digest URLs can be pre-filled with it).

Enhance the existing daily_flag_digest task in /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py (lines 10-38):
1. Group flags by target in the email body
2. Include pre-filled admin URLs with ?action= query param for quick triage

## Changes required

### 1. Add SITE_URL to /workspace/a_core/settings.py
Confirmed: SITE_URL does NOT currently exist in settings.py. Add:
  import os
  SITE_URL = os.environ.get('SITE_URL', 'http://localhost:8000')
Place near the top of settings, or alongside ALLOWED_HOSTS.

### 2. Group flags by target in daily_flag_digest
Current daily_flag_digest at line 10 of /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py builds a flat list. Replace with dict-accumulation grouping:

  from collections import defaultdict
  groups = defaultdict(list)
  for flag in unresolved[:50]:
      if flag.event:
          key = ('event', flag.event.pk, str(flag.event))
      elif flag.organizer:
          key = ('organizer', flag.organizer.pk, str(flag.organizer))
      elif flag.review:
          key = ('review', flag.review.pk, str(flag.review))
      else:
          key = ('unknown', 0, '(anonymous takedown)')
      groups[key].append(flag)

Then format the email body with one header per group:
  lines = [f'Unresolved flags: {count}\n']
  for (target_type, target_id, target_label), flags_in_group in groups.items():
      lines.append(f'\n{target_type.title()} "{target_label}" ({len(flags_in_group)} flags):')
      for flag in flags_in_group:
          admin_url = reverse('admin:reviews_flag_change', args=[flag.pk])
          suggested = _suggest_action(target_type, flag.reason)
          lines.append(f'  - [{flag.reason}] reporter: {flag.reporter or "anonymous"}')
          lines.append(f'    Admin: {settings.SITE_URL}{admin_url}?action={suggested}')

### 3. Suggested action helper
Add a small helper function in tasks_flags.py (not exported):
  def _suggest_action(target_type, reason):
      if target_type == 'review':
          return 'delete'
      if target_type == 'organizer' and reason == 'harmful':
          return 'suspend'
      return 'hide'

The suggested action is a convenience hint for the admin — the actual action is chosen in the admin UI.

### 4. Imports needed
  from collections import defaultdict
  from django.urls import reverse

## Key files
- /workspace/ingestion/tasks_flags.py (daily_flag_digest function lines 10-38; add _suggest_action)
- /workspace/a_core/settings.py (add SITE_URL — confirmed missing)

## Acceptance Criteria
- daily_flag_digest email body groups flags by target with count header per group
- Each flag entry includes full admin URL with ?action= pre-filled
- Test: mock 5 flags over 3 targets (2 event flags on event A, 2 event flags on event B, 1 review flag) → email body has 3 group headers with correct counts and admin URLs containing '?action='
- Admin URL resolves: reverse('admin:reviews_flag_change', args=[flag.pk]) does not raise NoReverseMatch
- SITE_URL appears in constructed admin URL

## Verification
  uv run pytest ingestion/tests/ -x -k 'digest'
  # Test: 5 flags across 3 targets → email body has 3 target group headers
  # Test: each group has admin URL containing '?action='
  # Test: SITE_URL appears in constructed admin URL

title: step-0: Test fixtures scaffold

Shared pytest fixtures for Bundle A tasks. Adds five reusable fixtures to /workspace/tests/conftest.py (extending the existing file, which already has superuser, staff_user, regular_user, approved_organizer, published_event). Drop this bead if step-1 and step-2 implementations prove no shared fixtures are needed.

NOTE: /workspace/reviews/tests.py already defines a local past_event fixture (line 48). The conftest versions below must use different names or be scoped to avoid conflicts. Prefer adding to conftest.py only if at least two other test files need the fixture; otherwise leave local.

## Fixtures to add to /workspace/tests/conftest.py

  user_with_went_attendance(event) — creates an approved User (is_approved=True) + Attendance(status='went', event=event). User model field: is_approved (not is_active).

  past_event_fixture(days_ago=N) — creates a published Event with end=timezone.now()-timedelta(days=N), organizer=approved_organizer. (Named past_event_fixture to avoid collision with local past_event in reviews/tests.py.)

  review_for_event_with_count(event, n) — creates n Review rows for event (with distinct author users each time), returns list. Uses event FK on Review model.

  organizer_with_rating_count(n) — creates Organizer + n Reviews via Review(organizer=org), then calls Organizer.objects.filter(pk=org.pk).update(rating_count=n) to denormalize.

  organizer_with_follower_count(n) — creates Organizer + n OrganizerFollow rows (one per distinct user), calls Organizer.objects.filter(pk=org.pk).update(follower_count=n).

## Key files
- /workspace/tests/conftest.py (extend — do not replace existing fixtures)
- /workspace/reviews/tests.py (reference for existing past_event fixture at line 48)
- /workspace/reviews/test_flags.py (reference for approved_user, client_approved fixture patterns)

## Acceptance Criteria
- All five fixtures are importable from tests/conftest.py with no test failures
- uv run pytest tests/ -x passes with fixtures loaded
- No fixture name collision with existing fixtures in the same conftest.py

## Verification
  uv run pytest tests/ -x --co -q
  uv run pytest tests/ -x
